I personally prefer KeePass, because it saves your database locally (and you can add another layer of authentication with a keyfile, which can be placed on an encrypted flash drive, which acts as a physical key to unlock your database)

I'm trying to chose between a 970 or a 290 and was wondering what everyone else was using.
What GPU are you using and what's your experience with it?

I have a pair of 970s in SLI, and I can't really complain. Overall, I'd pick the 970 over the 290. I'm satisfied with mine, it doesn't run too hot, and should you want to use Linux nVidia will be most performant on that platform too.

But the thing about the 290 is that it's cheaper, but is slightly worse or even equal in performance with the 970. Yes the 290 may run hotter and use more power, but I think its still a viable option.

Titan X. I love it. Upgraded from a 780ti and the difference is huge. I can play at higher resolutions (1440 vs 1080) with no drop in FPS, and even at 1080p the 780ti would sometimes get stuttering due to its 3GB memory, which the Titan's much larger memory eliminates.

I'm sure a 980ti would have sufficed and brought the same benefits, but I have no regrets going with this card.

gtx 980. When its running at stock clocks its not much better performance than my overclocked 780 but it is much much quieter. im really happy with it, i have a 1080p gsync monitor and i think anymore gpu power would be overkill. Ive tried sli and i really hate how some games dont work with sli so ill probably never use a multi card set up. I had a 290 in like 2013 but i wasnt impressed with it at all but i paid like $450 for it. if you can get one for around $200 its probably worth it for 60hz gaming but if you have 144hz monitor the 970 is the way to go.
would you say a 980 for 2 1080p monitors @ 60hz is overkill?
yea if you are gaming at 60hz then you can get a 290 for like $200

I'm currently running a 6950. Can't recommend it. I am in the same situtation as you in that I am comtemplating an upgrade. I might however wait for the Fury(X) or the Fury Nano to come out, as it is likely to lower prices for both camps, or in itself be something to consider.

EVGA GTX 550 Ti. Mad outdated but still a workhorse. Despite it's age, I can still play last gen bethesda games at high settings with graphics and lighting mods like mad. The only issues that pop up are fps loss (down to 30fps or so) and the fact that it is a freakin space heater. I need to upgrade it in the near future for something more heat efficient and powerful. Any suggestions? Budget is probably around 200 or less.
If you haven't bought yet, you now have the R9 390 Series to think about.

I personally have ASUS GTX670 DirectCu II(2GB VRAM version), been using it since release. Been serving me very well, cannot complain even a little.
We had an R9 290(Club3D RoyalAce) in another computer; we had to get the 290 refunded on warranty (unexplainable thermal issues, odd fan noise), got an ASUS GTX970 Strix as replacement. It's been working flawlessly; quiet, cool and powerful, cannot complain at all.

I'd wait and see how the AMD Fury series will perform. The Nano card intrigues me.

Between the 970 and 290, as it is now I'd personally take the 970 for the efficiency, even though I'm personally reluctant to give money to nvidia.
I've had my 7950 for over 2 years and have no plans to upgrade it works great.
I have a 660 3GB. It's pretty decent, I can run GTA V on high 1080 at 60fps.
R9 295x2. I love the power and when crossfire works, it is amazing. However, sometimes waiting for driver support or minor annoyances like flickering with Witcher 3 or Dyling Light put me off a tad.
EVGA GTX 670 - still runs the games i play at great settings with playable framerates (most even with 60). Will upgrade to a 970 though. But definitly EVGA again!

I've been on the 970 for around 8 months. I haven't manually overclocked it passed what MSI have done and I am still mostly maxing out triple A games. If I end up picking up a VR headset I might grab a second one to ensure I stay above 60fps and to utilize the GPU per eye feature that's part of the 900 series. Aside from that I couldn't be happier coming from an AMD 7770 before this.
Has the 3.5 vram been a issue at all while you've used it?

I'm still running a liquid cooled 6970. It can still play the latest games albeit not at the greatest settings. I'm getting to the point of upgrading but I'm not sure what to upgrade to yet. I'm waiting for the release of directX12 and seeing which gpu will perform the best price/value.

I am using a GTX 970 STRIX.

I have it at an overclock of +190 on the core clock and +400 on the memory. It seems to be very stable with the exception of playing Witcher 3. I generally add +10mv to add further stability for that game.

I put it on a static 65% fan rate. Temps stay below 68 degrees Celsius. It is generally very quiet.

With my overclock I can run essentially every single game I want to at whatever settings I want them at, @60fps. The only exceptions to this would be the new Batman, for obvious reasons, and Witcher 3 with Hairworks enabled.

I'm using a EVGA GTX 760. Even though I'm planning to upgrade to an R9 390 near the end of this month, I could probably still get a good 1 or 2 years of quality performance out of this card. It runs everything fantastically on high-ultra settings at or near 60FPS (i5 4690k, 16gb RAM). Mostly upgrading because I produce videos for some larger gaming sites, and need the extra performance.
